promo-plan-link.title: Two Canva links. One hands over your master file #shorts
promo-plan-link.description:
Canva's Template link means each buyer gets their own copy.

The edit link is the other one, and Canva's own words are that it "lets people make changes without signing up or logging in to Canva". They appear as guests — in YOUR design. There is only one of it.

Twelve buyers, one file. The first person who deletes a page deletes it for everyone, including the master you would need to fix it.

Check the URL says /template before you send it.

promo-plan-see-all.title: The Canva template link is hidden behind See all #shorts
promo-plan-see-all.description:
Share, then — and this is the bit people miss — if you do not see Template link, click See all. It is behind that. Then Create template link.

And Canva says creating a template link is only available on Pro, Teams, Enterprise, Education and Nonprofits. On the free plan the option is not there at all.

One more: delete a template link and Canva makes the URL inactive. Every buyer you have ever had is holding that link.

promo-plan-dates.title: Never reuse last year's planner file #shorts
promo-plan-dates.description:
The weekdays move. The first of January 2027 is a Friday — in 2026 it was a Thursday. Change the year on last year's file and every single date is wrong.

Three checks on every month: the 1st lands on the right weekday, the last day is right, and February has 28 days. 2027 is not a leap year.

It takes a minute and it prevents the one mistake buyers always spot.

promo-plan-sizes.title: US Letter and A4 are not the same page #shorts
promo-plan-sizes.description:
American buyers print on US Letter — eight and a half by eleven inches. Everywhere else prints on A4 — two hundred and ten by two hundred and ninety seven millimetres. A4 is narrower and taller.

A planner built only on Letter prints with a white stripe down one side and the bottom cut off, for half your customers.

Build both. Every listing, two files.
